**1 — Scene:** A tray meal that appears to contain chicken and rice in a yellow curry-style sauce, a brownie, and orange juice. I’m including the dessert and drink because both are fully visible on the same tray, rather than incidental food at the photo’s edge.

**2 — Vessels:** Main plate approximately **24 cm** across, area **452 cm²**; dessert plate approximately **20 cm**, area **314 cm²**. Glass internal diameter approximately **6 cm**, cross-sectional area **28 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Cooked rice, chicken pieces, yellow sauce, brownie with a light powdered-sugar topping, and orange juice. Sauce fat and brownie topping are included in their respective energy estimates.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy:** Rice, chicken, and sauce are intermingled, so their area shares are approximate allocations without double-counting.

| Item | Vessel area covered | Area × average height = volume | Density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Cooked rice | 30% of main plate | 136 × 1.6 = 218 ml | 0.8 | 174 g | 130 | 226 kcal |
| Chicken pieces | 20% of main plate | 90 × 1.7 = 153 ml | 0.95 | 145 g | 165 | 239 kcal |
| Yellow curry-style sauce | 15% of main plate | 68 × 0.8 = 54 ml | 1.0 | 54 g | 140 | 76 kcal |
| Brownie, including topping | 17% of dessert plate | 53 × 2.0 = 106 ml | 0.9 | 95 g | 430 | 409 kcal |
| Orange juice | 100% of glass cross-section | 28 × 9 = 252 ml | 1.04 | 262 g | 45 | 118 kcal |

Main-plate coverage totals **65%**; dessert-plate coverage is **17%**.

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **373 g** on the main plate is plausible for the visible mound. Including the substantial brownie and juice gives approximately **730 g and 1,070 kcal**. The sauce composition and brownie density are the largest uncertainties.
